title: When the Radiators Breaks
premise: Ulyana Blackwood, a piano tuner who reads a house's history through the sounds of its radiators, is hired to prepare the old Kestrel house for sale and discovers its pipes still carry fragments of Vessic, a dying language once spoken there. The last fluent speaker, an elderly caretaker named Tomas Veren, asks her to become his final student before the house — and with it the language's last living archive — passes to developers. As Ulyana learns, she uncovers that her own mother helped silence Vessic decades ago during a bitter estate dispute, and that Tomas has been waiting not for a student but for an heir to an apology. When the sale closes early, Ulyana must choose between letting the house go quietly or publicly contesting it with what she knows; in the end she records Tomas's final telling of the story in Vessic, lets the house be sold, and carries the language forward as its second-to-last speaker turned first teacher.
about_author: R. M. Yarrow is the pen name of a former building conservator who spent fifteen years cataloguing historic homes across the northern counties. Their fiction explores how ordinary objects hold the debts families refuse to pay.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Hired to tune the Kestrel house's ancient steam radiators before its sale, she catalogs each pipe's voice — knocks, hisses, a rhythm like speech. She notes her habit of keeping mental inventories of everything people don't say, including her estranged mother's silence about this town. Beat: wary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: What the Pipes Remember
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. In the basement she hears a pattern too structured to be mechanical and records it on her phone. The caretaker, Tomas Veren, appears at the door and identifies it as Vessic — a lullaby sung into the pipes by children decades ago. He reveals fewer than a handful of speakers remain. Beat: wonder cracking open routine.

chapters.title: One Final Student
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Tomas offers to teach her Vessic before the sale erases the house's acoustic archive. She resists — she tunes pianos, she doesn't inherit causes — but the recorded lullaby won't leave her head. First lesson: he teaches her the word for 'listen' before any word for 'speak.' Beat: reluctant commitment.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Cooling House
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana and Tomas POVs. Winter lessons among draining radiators; each drained pipe silences part of the archive. Tomas teaches through objects and rooms rather than grammar. Ulyana begins hearing her own childhood in the sounds. Beat: intimacy deepening alongside loss.

chapters.title: The Mother's Signature
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Sorting estate papers for the sale, Ulyana finds her mother's name on the 1980s documents that transferred Vessic-speaking tenants out of the house — testimony signed against them. Confronted, her mother admits she traded testimony for housing security after Ulyana's father left. Beat: betrayal reframing everything.

chapters.title: Tomas Already Knew
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Flashback chapters braided in: young Tomas watching the eviction hearings, recognizing Ulyana's mother as the neighbor who looked away. Present-day Tomas confesses he sought out Ulyana deliberately — the student request was also a summons. Ulyana feels used. Beat: trust fractured at midpoint.

chapters.title: Closing Date
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The developer accelerates the sale; demolition of interior fixtures, including radiators, moves up. Ulyana must decide whether to file a heritage objection using her mother's documents — exposing her family — or stay silent and keep learning. Her mother begs her to let the past stay buried. Beat: pressure mounting from all sides.

chapters.title: The Last Full Telling
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Tomas POVs. Before the pipes are cut, Tomas performs the complete oral history of the house in Vessic, recorded in one night. Halfway through, Ulyana realizes she understands without translation. She responds in Vessic — her first full sentences — and forgives him, though not yet herself. Beat: climax of inheritance.

chapters.title: Objection
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At the closing, Ulyana doesn't stop the sale but enters the recording and documents into the public record, naming her mother's role aloud. The sale proceeds; the house falls to the developers, but the language's existence is now legally and culturally acknowledged. Her mother walks out; Ulyana lets her go. Beat: costly, imperfect victory.

chapters.title: Second Speaker
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, epilogue tone. Spring: the house is gutted, but Ulyana salvages one radiator and installs it in her workshop, where it ticks in Vessic rhythms. She posts her first lesson online and receives a reply from a stranger whose grandmother spoke Vessic. The inventory of unsaid things finally has an entry marked 'said.' Beat: quiet, earned hope.
